Surgical Breast Enlargement

Mastectomy & Chest Contouring Surgery: Patient Information

Mastectomy removes breast tissue. When performed to create a flatter, more contoured chest, it is often called chest masculinisation or top surgery.

Home/Surgical Breast Enlargement/Mastectomy & Chest Contouring Surgery: Patient Information

Mastectomy is the surgical removal of breast tissue. It is performed for several reasons, including gender-affirming chest masculinisation, reduction of elevated cancer risk in selected patients, and treatment of disease. This page provides general educational information; the appropriate procedure, eligibility and timing are determined through individual medical assessment.

When the goal is chest contouring rather than treatment of disease, the technique is tailored to the amount of breast tissue, skin laxity and the desired chest shape. Approaches may include a double-incision technique with nipple grafting, or a periareolar (keyhole) approach in suitable anatomy. The surgeon also considers scar placement, chest-wall contour and future revision options.

What to discuss

Questions for your consultation

Which technique suits you

The approach depends on tissue volume, skin elasticity and the contour you want.

Scars and nipple position

Where incisions fall and how nipple–areola position and sensation are planned.

Risks

Bleeding, infection, contour irregularity, sensation changes and the possibility of revision.

Recovery

Drain use, compression garments, activity restrictions and follow-up schedule.

Eligibility assessment

Medical and psychological assessment where required, and any eligibility criteria that apply.

Future procedures

Whether staged or additional surgery may be needed to refine the result.

Assessment comes first

Chest surgery is elective and requires assessment by an appropriately qualified surgeon, including a discussion of risks, alternatives, realistic outcomes and — where required — eligibility criteria. No outcome can be guaranteed.

Questions

Mastectomy & chest surgery FAQs

Breast reduction removes a portion of tissue to make the breasts smaller while preserving a feminine breast shape. Mastectomy for chest contouring removes breast tissue to create a flatter, more masculine chest wall, with a different approach to nipple position and scars.

Most people are satisfied with a single procedure, but refinement or revision surgery is sometimes desired for contour or scar reasons. This is discussed in advance.

Recovery varies with the technique and individual healing. Compression garments, limited arm activity and drain care are commonly required for a period after surgery, with a gradual return to full activity as advised by your surgeon.
